title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page has nothing to do with the divided-power de Rham notes around it. It is a typewritten exam or exercise sheet, 'Problème MP 2', probably a teaching document from Grothendieck's Montpellier years (or a colleague's), with typed-over corrections, reused or filed among the notes. The neighbouring pages are about graded C-S-modules, truncation functors tau_N and localisation; there is no mathematical link.

The exercise aims to study the convergence of series sum u_n/n with (u_n) bounded complex, and to compute their sums when u_n is periodic of period r.

Part I a) is Dirichlet's test proved by Abel summation. Let (c_n) be decreasing, positive and tending to 0, and let the partial sums S_n = sum_{1<=i<=n} u_i satisfy |S_n| <= M. Then sum u_n c_n converges, with a bound on the tail R_n = sum_{i>=n+1} u_i c_i. The hint is the Cauchy criterion on sum_{n<i<=m} u_i c_i, using u_i = S_i - S_{i-1}.

Part I b): for r-periodic u, if sum c_n converges then sum u_n c_n converges for every periodic u. If sum c_n diverges, then sum u_n c_n converges iff sum_{i=1}^r u_i = 0. The proof splits u = (constant) + (zero-mean periodic) uniquely and applies a) to the zero-mean part, whose partial sums are bounded.

Part I c): E_r is the complex vector space of r-periodic sequences with zero mean over a period (condition (3)); it has dimension r-1. For fixed n_0 >= 1 and 1 <= s <= r-1, u(s) is the element of E_r equal to 1 at n_0, -1 at n_0+s, and 0 at the other positions of that period. One must show that the u(s) form a basis of E_r. Presumably the sequel computes sum u(s)_n/n as a telescoping or log-type quantity. Summing over residues then gives sum u_n/n = -(1/r) sum_a u_a psi(a/r), equivalently a linear combination of logs of cyclotomic numbers. These are Gauss's digamma theorem and L(1,chi) territory.
errors: The tail bound as typed, |R_n| <= M c_{n+1} (and the Cauchy-step bound |sum_{n<i<=m} u_i c_i| <= M c_{n+1}), is false in general. Abel summation gives S_m c_m - S_n c_{n+1} + sum_{i=n+1}^{m-1} S_i (c_i - c_{i+1}), which is bounded by 2M c_{n+1}. Counterexample: u = (-1, 2, -2, 2, ...), so that |S_n| <= 1, with c_2 large relative to the later c_i; then R_1 is close to 2c_2. The constant should be 2M, unless the bound is meant for S_n starting at the index n.
The hint says 'remplacer c_i par S_i - S_{i-1}'; it should be u_i.
In the introduction, 'u_{n+r} = u_n pour tout r' should read 'pour tout n'.
'Pour tout entier n >= 0' while S_n is a sum over 1 <= i <= n; this is harmless (S_0 = 0).
'Condition (3)' refers to the unnumbered displayed condition sum_{1<=i<=r} u_i = 0.

ideas.what: Abel summation / Dirichlet test with explicit tail bound
ideas.modern_name: Dirichlet's test, Abel summation by parts

ideas.what: Convergence of sum u_n c_n for periodic u iff zero mean (when sum c_n diverges), via splitting into constant plus zero-mean part
Basis of zero-mean r-periodic sequences by 'difference of two Dirac' sequences, aimed at computing sum u_n/n

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine undergraduate analysis exercise (Dirichlet test, periodic series), unrelated to the surrounding research notes. Its only interest is as evidence of Grothendieck's (or a colleague's) Montpellier teaching material. It contains a minor error in a constant.
transcription_corrections: The missing symbols are summation signs and inequality signs: 'S_n = sum_{1<=i<=n} u_i', '|S_n| <= M', 'M >= 0', 'n >= 0', '(c_n)_{n>=1}', 'm >= n', 'r >= 1', '1 <= s <= r-1', '0 <= i <= r-1', 'u(s) in E_r'. The convergence statements involve sum u_n/n, sum u_n c_n, |R_n| <= M c_{n+1}, and |sum_{n<i<=m} u_i c_i| <= M c_{n+1} (the inequality signs are lost in the typescript).
The displayed series at the top is 'sum u_n/n'.
The struck text 'xxxxxxxxxxxx' is a typed-over line; 'a)' was moved from the margin to before 'positifs'.
